raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Pont Neuf behind, head for the Square du Vert-Galant, just ahead.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"See the king on horseback back on the bridge? That's Henri IV, who loved this city mightily — its wine, its women, its good times — and the leafy triangular square below him carries his name.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Vert-Galant means the green, or lusty, gallant, a nod to a love life so legendary the whole garden became a haunt of lovers.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262","af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049"]},{"text":"You reach it by the steps behind his statue, down into the triangular western tip of this boat-shaped island.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262"]},{"text":"This is where Paris began, the settlement of a Celtic tribe called the Parisii that Caesar subdued.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The Romans named it Lutetia, and in 358 the emperor Julian called it Cara Lutetia — \"my beloved Lutetia.\"","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Centuries later, as king from 1589 to 1610, Henri set out to make this city, in his own words, \"a whole world\" and \"a wonder of the world.\"","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"He mostly delivered — the Pont Neuf you just crossed, the \"new bridge\" that's actually the oldest in Paris, was his, and so were the Place Dauphine and the Place Royale, the square we now call the Place des Vosges.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"His private life was busier still: two wives, at least fifty-six mistresses, and households full of children born out of wedlock.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"At first the Parisians adored him for it, but the charm faded as he aged, and his dozens of scattered bastards began to grate — enough that France nearly slid back into civil strife.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3"]},{"text":"Worse, he meant to marry his favourite, Gabrielle d'Estrées, an outrage to the reasons of state — only her sudden death spared the kingdom the scandal.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"As Femme Ladoucette wrote to the Queen, in the kingdom of France one keeps the sheep apart from the goats.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And yet, above all the scandal, Henri was a peacemaker.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Raised a strict Protestant, he converted to Catholicism, the faith of the majority, to end the religious wars that by the close of the sixteenth century had left Paris starving and looking like a bomb site.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Then, hating the partisanship, he signed the Edict of Nantes in 1598, writing tolerance for the very faith he'd abandoned into law.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It didn't save him. A fanatical Catholic named Francis Ravaillac stabbed him to death, unpersuaded by any of it.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Even so, alongside Charlemagne, Joan of Arc, and Saint Louis, Henri IV is still counted among France's heroes — a king who called kindness and mercy the first virtues of a prince.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"These days the prime spot is the tree-dotted knoll right at the point, where the river boats still dock along the north side.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"From here the view is unforgettable — the Hôtel de la Monnaie and the dome of the Institut de France to your left, the Louvre to your right, the Pont-des-Arts straight ahead.","source_id":"391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Come back after dark. It's pure enchantment.","source_id":"391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1}]}
